Author: Tensho
Name: Tensho Assistant
Description:
Everyday tools in one window (/tensho), with a guide and help on every page.

Items and storage (bags, retainers, saddlebags, armoury chest, glamour dresser, armoire), inventory
sorting rules, market listings and prices, retainer sale prices compared on a click, recipes, a crafting
simulator and solver, gathering and fishing with Eorzea time windows and weather, a map that replaces
the game map (quests, leves, FATEs, gathering points, vendors, aether currents, teleport costs), weather,
alarms and reminders, free company voyages and builds, quests and rewards, collections with how to
obtain each item, a gear planner (materia, try on, build sharing), duty and monster loot, Beastmaster
information, Fashion Report hints, Mini Cactpot, Triple Triad helpers (against NPCs only), character
stats, macro chains and a Credits page listing every source.

Network: community data (Universalis, Garland Tools, FFXIV Console Games Wiki, Teamcraft bite times,
PaissaDB open plots, and files hosted on GitHub: LuminaSupplemental, GatherBuddy, FFXIVGachaSpreadsheet; the shared discoveries exchange through your GitHub account, only after you connect it)
is requested over HTTPS only when you open or hover the matching tool, click, or a setting asks for it,
with bounded replies and a disk cache. Each source has a switch in Settings > Advanced. This plugin's own
repository is read on a click for the gallery of community tools (data only, no code) and the help
videos. Nothing about your character is sent, except on options that are off by default: posting Tensho
alarms and currency cap alerts to a Discord webhook you enter, with your character's name only if you ask
for it. An item's page on the wiki or the Lodestone, and partake.gg (player events), open in your browser
only on a click or a /tensho command. Reporting a problem opens a prefilled form in your browser; you read
it and send it yourself.

Actions that reach the game (teleport, applying a sort, a macro chain, writing crafting macros, opening
Try On, equipping a gear set, sending the hunt train call to the chat channel you choose) start only when you click them. Game
alarms are created with /alarm when you add an alarm with the « game alarms » setting on (off by default)
or press Send. One setting, off by default, acts without a click: wearing the title you chose for a job
when you change job. No automation of crafting, dialogues or loot, no PvP feature, no parser.

AI disclosure: the code and the icon were generated with an AI coding agent (Claude), directed and tested
in game by the author.

Languages: English and French; German and Japanese: menu titles only.
Punchline: One window for everyday tools: items, crafting, gathering, map, collections and more.

## 0.1172.0
- Tensho's visual sort of the bags (Items › Organisation): the sorted items fill the bags in the order 1, 3, 2, 4 instead of 1, 2, 3, 4, so the order reads coherently on the game's screen (X-187, user request of 11/12). The preview shows the same placement. Zones keep the positions they name; only the items outside the zones follow the new order. The other storages (retainers, saddlebags) do not change.

## 0.1171.0
- GitHub exchange of the discoveries, GitHub App token (X-181, findings N2, N7, N8, N29 and N30 of the night review of 11/12). Two game clients renewing the token at once no longer sign each other out: one renewal at a time per profile (shared lock file); under that lock the files are read again and a pair already renewed by the other client is taken without asking GitHub again; a refusal signs out only when the files still hold the refused token, never the other client's new pair. « Disconnect » during a renewal: nothing is kept, no token file comes back, nothing is sent afterwards. A renewal GitHub accepted is no longer lost: its request has its own deadline, independent of the plugin's stop (unloading waits a few seconds for it); the pair is kept in memory first, then written, and a refused write is retried before the next use. A 401 answer with a refresh token in hand: one forced renewal and one more upload before signing out. After reconnecting with another GitHub account, a gist and an issue of that account's own (the gist's login is noted). Fix of X-182 (0.1169), found by the CI of 0.1170: a second client loading during the conversion no longer fails when the first moves the old file under it (nothing is written, the other's conversion holds); the behaviour test replays it 20 times.

## 0.1170.0
- Shared discoveries, v3 exchange format: the plugin now ignores a field it does not know when it reads the common file (v3/), instead of refusing the line; a field added later will therefore not need a version 4 (X-186, user's choice of 11/12, finding N31 of the night review). A line holding Own or Key (a player's own part, the only privacy-related fields), in any case, is still refused whole. The merge tool stays strict on the players' gists (any other name refuses the line). The community-discoveries README says so, in English and French.

## 0.1169.0
- Player data: two game clients, or two versions of the plugin the same day, no longer erase each other's data (X-182, in part; findings N3, N4, N9, N11, N27 and N28 of the night review of 11/12). Submarine and airship voyages: each save writes only the voyages that changed, by their key, never emptying the table; two clients on two companies keep each other's voyages; voyages older than 180 days (and beyond 5,000) are removed apart. Achievements: each reading replaces the saved one only when newer; a client left open no longer takes back from the other what it saw since. A file of before (voyages, achievements, gil journal) written again after the conversion by an older version still running is merged, no longer set aside unread; a copy already set aside is not read again. The conversion reads the file of before in an immediate transaction: a second client loading at the same time waits, then sees everything. A file of before is moved only once the database is written to the disk (full checkpoint), else at the next start. Conversion of the discoveries: a temporary name of its own for each conversion, never removed by another instance; the first whole base stays. Left of X-182: the bank (file written again after the conversion, the « unchanged » decision taken from memory) and a discoveries file written again after the conversion.

## 0.1165.0
- Gardening: tending done in game updates the right bed (X-179, user's finding of 11/12: « manual tending does not update the alarms »). ## 0.1164.0
- Hitches (X-177, step 2): the settings are saved off the game's thread. The measuring lines of 0.1162 show that Dalamud's save of the settings took 64 to 71 ms on the game's thread each time, and 371 to 648 ms the first time after a load, while turning the settings into text takes about 2 ms (measured on a copy of the user's settings, 63 KB). Now only the text is made on the game's thread; a copy of it is rebuilt apart, checked (it must give back exactly the same text, otherwise it is not written) and saved off the game's thread. One write at a time, in order, the latest only: an older write never lands after a newer one. At the slightest doubt (different copy, refused write), Tensho goes back to the old way, on the game's thread, and says so once in the log. When the plugin stops, what is left is written. The text maker is warmed at load off the game's thread, so the first save is not slow. The three other direct saves (alarm sources, confirmed weather zones, today's Grand Company request) go the same way. The other hitches seen today (readers, reminder bar) only happen when the plugin loads.

## 0.1163.0
- Beast labyrinth: the board's result (X-135, user request). At the end of a board, Tensho reads the game's result window (its numbers only, never its texts): the score, then each team beast's rank and experience before and after. The values were established on the board the user played on 11/12 in developer mode (the « before » values are those the game's bestiary showed before the board). The last result is kept with the teams: Beastmaster › Team shows it (ranks gained in green), and the « after » ranks replace the known ones, so the advised team is worked out again with them; the beast list shows each beast's known rank. A window that does not match what was seen (score not the sum of its parts, unknown beast, rank going down, experience outside 0 to 100) is refused whole: nothing is kept rather than a wrong rank. Ranks read in the team window before the page was opened are no longer lost. The loot (booty and treasure windows) is decoded in the evidence but not shown yet: the game already shows it.
